items.q: A 12 Ω resistor is in series with a parallel pair of 6 Ω and 12 Ω. The circuit is connected to 48 V. What is the total current?
items.explain: Parallel pair: (6 × 12) / 18 = 4 Ω. Total = 12 + 4 = 16 Ω. I = 48 / 16 = 3 A.

items.q: A 40 Ω heating element is connected across 120 V. How much power does it dissipate?
A 208 V three-phase feeder carries 50 A over 150 ft (one way) on 6 AWG copper (26,240 cmil). Using K = 12.9, the approximate voltage drop is:
A 240 V single-phase circuit carries 30 A for 200 ft (one way). To hold voltage drop to 3% (7.2 V) with K = 12.9, the minimum copper conductor is:
items.explain: Required CM = 2 × K × I × L / VD = 2 × 12.9 × 30 × 200 / 7.2 ≈ 21,500 cmil. 8 AWG (16,510) is too small; 6 AWG (26,240) is the first size that qualifies.

items.q: A 120 V single-phase circuit carries 20 A for 100 ft (one way) on 10 AWG aluminum (10,380 cmil). Using K = 21.2 for aluminum, the voltage drop is approximately:
items.explain: VD = 2 × 21.2 × 20 × 100 / 10,380 ≈ 8.2 V (about 6.8%). Aluminum's K is roughly 1.6 × copper's, which is why aluminum runs need larger sizes for the same drop.

items.q: A balanced 480 V three-phase load draws 40 A per line. What is its apparent power?
A 75 kVA three-phase transformer is fed at 480 V. What is its full-load primary line current?
A 45 kVA three-phase transformer has a 208Y/120 V secondary. Its full-load secondary line current is approximately:
A single-phase transformer steps 7,200 V down to 240 V. When the secondary delivers 100 A, the primary current is approximately:
items.explain: Turns ratio = 7,200 / 240 = 30:1. Current is inversely proportional: 100 / 30 ≈ 3.3 A. Check: 7,200 × 3.33 ≈ 240 × 100 = 24 kVA.

items.q: Adding capacitors in parallel with an inductive motor load will:
choices: Raise the power factor and reduce line current
items.explain: Capacitive VAR cancels inductive VAR, so apparent power (and line current) drops while true power stays the same.

items.q: A load draws 10 kVA and consumes 8 kW. What is its reactive power?
items.explain: VAR = √(kVA² − kW²) = √(100 − 64) = 6 kVAR. Power factor here is 0.8.

items.q: A 240 V RMS sine wave has an approximate peak-to-peak value of:
Chapter 9 Table 8 lists 10 AWG uncoated copper at about 1.2 Ω per 1,000 ft. The resistance of a 500 ft length is approximately:
items.explain: Resistance is proportional to length: 1.2 Ω × (500 / 1,000) = 0.6 Ω.

items.q: A 15 kW, 480 V three-phase resistive heater draws what line current?
A 5 hp motor operating at 83% efficiency runs fully loaded for 10 hours. Approximately how much energy does it consume?
Two resistors in series across 120 V draw 2 A. One resistor is 20 Ω. The other is:
A 10 Ω and a 30 Ω resistor are in parallel and the total current is 12 A. How much current flows through the 10 Ω resistor?
items.explain: Current divides inversely with resistance: I(10 Ω) = 12 × 30 / (10 + 30) = 9 A; the 30 Ω branch carries 3 A. Check: 9 × 10 = 3 × 30 = 90 V across both.

items.q: After a capacitor in a DC circuit is fully charged, it behaves like:
choices: A resistor equal to its reactance
items.explain: Once charged to the source voltage, no further current flows — an open circuit to DC. Capacitors pass changing (AC) current, block steady DC.

items.q: A balanced delta-connected load draws 52 A of line current. The current in each phase winding is approximately:
items.explain: Delta: I(phase) = I(line) / 1.732 = 52 / 1.732 ≈ 30 A.

items.q: On a 208Y/120 V 4-wire system with linear loads, phase A carries 30 A, phase B carries 30 A, and phase C carries 0 A. The neutral current is:
items.explain: In = √(A² + B² + C² − AB − BC − CA) = √(900 + 900 + 0 − 900 − 0 − 0) = √900 = 30 A. With two phases equally loaded, the neutral carries the same as one phase.

items.q: A 240 V circuit supplies a 4,800 W resistive load through conductors with a total round-trip resistance of 0.2 Ω. The voltage drop in the conductors is approximately:
items.explain: Load current ≈ 4,800 / 240 = 20 A. VD = I × R = 20 × 0.2 = 4 V. (Strictly the current is slightly higher after the drop, but 4 V is the exam answer.)

items.q: A 120 V circuit supplies a 10 Ω resistive load. What current flows?
A 240 V, single-phase resistive heater draws 20 A. What is its power?
A 1,200 W heating element is rated for 120 V. What is its resistance?
Resistors of 10 Ω, 20 Ω, and 30 Ω are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
items.explain: Series resistances add: 10 + 20 + 30 = 60 Ω.

items.q: Two 30 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
items.explain: Equal resistors in parallel: R / n = 30 / 2 = 15 Ω.

items.q: A 10 Ω and a 20 Ω resistor are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
Resistors of 10 Ω, 20 Ω, and 30 Ω in series are connected across 120 V. What is the voltage across the 30 Ω resistor?
items.explain: Total R = 60 Ω, so I = 120 / 60 = 2 A. Voltage across 30 Ω = 2 × 30 = 60 V.

items.q: At any junction in a circuit, the sum of currents entering equals the sum of currents leaving. This is:
items.explain: Kirchhoff's current law: charge is conserved at a node. The voltage law says voltage drops around a closed loop sum to the source voltage.

items.q: A sine-wave voltage reads 120 V RMS on a meter. What is its approximate peak value?
A 60 Hz AC supply completes how many full cycles in one second?
items.explain: Hertz = cycles per second. 60 Hz = 60 cycles each second (120 alternations).

items.q: An AC circuit has 30 Ω of resistance and 40 Ω of inductive reactance in series. What is the impedance?
items.explain: Z = √(R² + X²) = √(900 + 1,600) = √2,500 = 50 Ω. Resistance and reactance add as vectors, not arithmetically.

items.q: A motor circuit uses 2,400 W of true power while drawing 3,000 VA of apparent power. What is the power factor?
A 240 V single-phase load draws 25 A. What is the apparent power?
A balanced three-phase, 208 V load draws 30 A per line at unity power factor. What is the power?
On a 480Y/277 V system, what is the relationship between 480 V and 277 V?
choices: 277 V is half of 480 V plus a safety margin
277 V is the delta phase voltage
items.explain: In a wye, line-to-line voltage = line-to-neutral × 1.732. 480 / 1.732 ≈ 277 V.

items.q: In a balanced delta-connected load, line current equals:
items.explain: Delta: line voltage = phase voltage, line current = √3 × phase current. Wye is the reverse.

items.q: A transformer steps 480 V down to 120 V. What is its turns ratio (primary:secondary)?
items.explain: Voltage ratio equals turns ratio: 480 / 120 = 4, so 4:1.

items.q: A 10 kVA single-phase transformer has a 240 V secondary. What is the full-load secondary current?
A 25 kVA three-phase transformer has a 208Y/120 V secondary. What is the full-load secondary line current?
One horsepower is equal to approximately how many watts?
items.explain: 1 hp = 746 W. A 5 hp output is about 3,730 W.

items.q: A 5 hp motor operates at 85% efficiency. What is its approximate input power?
items.explain: Output = 5 × 746 = 3,730 W. Input = output / efficiency = 3,730 / 0.85 ≈ 4,388 W.

items.q: A 120 V single-phase branch circuit runs 100 ft (one way) on 12 AWG copper (6,530 cmil) and carries 16 A. Using K = 12.9, what is the approximate voltage drop?
items.explain: VD = 2 × K × I × L / CM = 2 × 12.9 × 16 × 100 / 6,530 ≈ 6.3 V (about 5.3% — above the 3% branch-circuit recommendation).

items.q: The NEC informational note recommends limiting branch-circuit voltage drop to what percentage for reasonable efficiency of operation?
items.explain: Recommendation (not a requirement): 3% on the branch circuit and 5% total for feeder plus branch circuit.

items.q: If the length of a conductor is doubled (same material and size), its resistance:
items.explain: Resistance is directly proportional to length and inversely proportional to cross-sectional area.

items.q: In a 120/240 V single-phase, 3-wire circuit, line A carries 20 A and line B carries 14 A. What does the neutral carry?
items.explain: On a single-phase 3-wire system the neutral carries the unbalance: 20 − 14 = 6 A.

items.q: In a perfectly balanced three-phase, 4-wire wye system supplying linear loads, the neutral current is:
items.explain: Balanced three-phase currents are 120° apart and cancel in the neutral. Nonlinear (harmonic) loads can change that.

items.q: If the frequency applied to an inductor increases, its inductive reactance:
items.explain: XL = 2πfL — reactance rises with frequency. Capacitive reactance does the opposite.

items.q: As frequency increases, the capacitive reactance of a capacitor:
items.explain: XC = 1 / (2πfC) — higher frequency, lower reactance.

items.q: A 1,500 W heater runs 8 hours a day for 30 days. At $0.15 per kWh, what does it cost?
As the temperature of a copper conductor rises, its resistance:
items.explain: Copper has a positive temperature coefficient. This is why ampacity tables carry temperature correction factors.

items.q: Three 60 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. What is the total resistance?
items.explain: Equal resistors in parallel: 60 / 3 = 20 Ω.

items.q: A current of 5 A flows through an 8 Ω resistor. How much power is dissipated?
Two 20 Ω resistors in parallel are connected in series with a 10 Ω resistor across 120 V. What is the total current?
items.explain: Parallel pair = 10 Ω; total = 10 + 10 = 20 Ω; I = 120 / 20 = 6 A.

items.q: A wattmeter connected to an AC circuit measures:
items.explain: A wattmeter responds to voltage × current × power factor — true power. VA requires separate voltage and current readings.

items.q: A voltage is induced in a conductor when it:
choices: Cuts through magnetic lines of force
items.explain: Faraday's law of induction — the basis of generators and transformers. Relative motion (or changing flux) between conductor and field induces voltage.

items.q: A three-phase, 208 V load draws 50 A per line. What transformer kVA is needed (minimum, at full load)?
In a purely inductive AC circuit, the current:
choices: Is in phase with the voltage
items.explain: ELI the ICE man: in an inductor (L), voltage (E) leads current (I); in a capacitor (C), current leads voltage.

items.q: A 7.2 kW resistive heater operates at 240 V single-phase. What current does it draw?
The DC resistance of 1,000 ft of 12 AWG uncoated copper at 75°C is approximately:
items.explain: Chapter 9, Table 8 lists roughly 1.9–2.0 Ω per 1,000 ft for 12 AWG copper. Each three sizes smaller roughly doubles the resistance.

items.q: A motor delivers 10 hp while drawing 9 kW from the line. What is its efficiency?
In a wye-connected load, the line current is:
items.explain: Wye: line current = phase current; line voltage = √3 × phase voltage.

items.q: A 15 kVA single-phase load at 240 V draws what current?
A three-phase, 480 V feeder runs 250 ft on 1/0 AWG copper (105,600 cmil) at 100 A. Using K = 12.9, the approximate voltage drop is:
In a series circuit, which quantity is the same through every component?
items.explain: Only one path exists, so current is identical everywhere. Voltage divides across the components.
